thread:
marina: heads-up — acme-pay reported a sudden spike of 429s in production around 18:02 UTC. They say it started after a marketing push, traffic up ~6x for a few minutes. can someone triage?

devin: on it. can you paste an example request id / time window? also ask them if they see X-RateLimit headers in responses (we sometimes still return them for quota hits).

marina: posted sample response from their logs: `{"error":"Too Many Requests","code":429}`. no headers shown in the dump they sent. window: 18:01:30–18:04:10.

devin: stepping through our edge logs for that window. quick note: customer is on hosted tier with default RPM/TPM caps (300 RPM / 6000 TPM) — marketing could blow that.

jules: if it's a short burst, it's likely RPM (per-minute) hitting. TPM affects sustained throughput. do we have per-customer meter logs for that account?

devin: yes pulling meter: `acct:acme-pay` shows 310 requests in minute starting 18:02, 3.5k token bursts in that 60s slice. we returned 429s at edge for ~45s. correlating with our ratecap module logs now.

marina: customer says they didn't change client. they blamed our API. want guidance asap — they have live customers impacted.

devin: posting relevant snippet from ratecap logs (redacted):
```
[2026-07-15T18:02:05Z] ratecap: acct=acme-pay limit=300 window=60s count=301 action=throttle code=RPM_EXCEEDED
[2026-07-15T18:02:06Z] ratecap: acct=acme-pay limit=300 window=60s count=322 action=throttle
[2026-07-15T18:02:30Z] ratecap: acct=acme-pay backoff_until=2026-07-15T18:03:10Z
```

jules: confirms RPM exceeded. what about retries? if their client retried aggressively they could amplify.

marina: they said their mobile clients retry every 1s with linear backoff, no jitter.

sandeep: that pattern explains pressure. immediate guidance we should give customer: 1) implement exponential backoff + full jitter (e.g., base=0.5s, cap=10s), 2) honor 429 and `Retry-After` header, 3) reduce client burst (leaky bucket client-side), 4) consider batching or queuing during marketing spikes.

devin: we should also suggest short-term mitigations we can do on our side: a) increase RPM for them temporarily if account qualifies (ops-approved), b) enable soft-burst windowing for 5m (risk: transient cost), c) advise using Dedicated or higher tier for expected traffic surges.

marina: asked customer whether they can pause the push — they can't. they want us to raise limits now. any safety checks before we bump?

jules: checklist before increasing: - confirm caller identity/authorization - ensure no misbehaving client (infinite retry loop) - check downstream model capacity and latency SLOs - set a temporary TTL bump and auto-revert (15m) - notify SRE oncall

devin: audit shows no infinite loops — their SDK version 1.2.1 has 1s retry, but only up to 4 attempts. that's still too aggressive for a mass push.

marina: I drafted a message to customer with both short-term and long-term recommendations. will run it by eng.

sandeep: add an explicit code snippet for clients, makes it easier for them to patch quickly. here's a minimal JS exponential backoff example: 
```js
async function callWithBackoff(fn, attempts=6) {
  for (let i=0;i<attempts;i++){
    try { return await fn(); }
    catch (err) {
      if (err.status !== 429) throw err;
      const base = 500; // ms
      const cap = 10000; // ms
      const jitter = Math.random();
      const delay = Math.min(cap, base * Math.pow(2,i)) * jitter;
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, delay));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('retries exhausted');
}
```

jules: also include sample curl + header check so they can confirm server headers: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \ 
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# look for: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `Retry-After`
```

devin: note: our edge may not return `X-RateLimit` headers in all failure modes; we will try to surface `Retry-After` consistently. filed internal ticket INF-814 to normalize headers.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-314 (rate-limit spike for acct=acme-pay). Pager duty notified.

marina: customer replied — they see `Retry-After: 30` on a subset of failed responses. good. they asked for a temporary bump to 900 RPM for the next 20 minutes.

jules: bump ok if SRE approves and we apply an auto-revert. i'm +1 but need oncall explicit approval.

devin: oncall (sylvia) paged, sylvia approved a 900 RPM soft bump for 20m — applied with an audit note. monitoring alerted if CPU or latency > 2x baseline.

marina: sent customer update: we increased RPM to 900 for 20m, asked them to implement backoff + jitter and report after campaign.

sandeep: follow-ups for product/docs: - add client guidance in support KB about handling mass marketing spikes - publish best-practice retry snippets across SDKs - doc on how to request temporary limit increases (include auto-revert and safety checks)

jules: ops note: we should add a ratecap metric that surfaces per-account minute-overhead bursts (p90 burstiness) to proactively warn for customers trending towards limits. filing INF-822.

devin: closing loop: root cause = RPM exceeded due to marketing-driven burst + client retry pattern. mitigation = temporary RPM bump + customer-side backoff + product follow-ups. will attach logs and ticket numbers to support case.

marina: thanks all. assigning a follow-up to sandeep to push KB update and to jules for infra metrics.

sandeep: ack. i'll draft the KB with code samples and a short troubleshooting checklist: check headers, reproduce with replayed traffic, recommend Dedicated if recurring.

marina: case updated, closing thread once KB & infra tickets filed. :thumbsup:
